questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Improving Workflow Reliability?
options: Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Reliable workflows use deterministic dependency versions, explicit timeouts, idempotent deployment steps, bounded retries, and tested recovery paths.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
questions.answer_key: Reliable workflows use deterministic dependency versions, explicit timeouts, idempotent deployment steps, bounded retries, and tested recovery paths.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of improving workflow reliability: Reliable workflows use deterministic dependency versions, explicit timeouts, idempotent deployment steps, bounded retries, and tested recovery paths. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: A team is working with “Deterministic build steps”. Which practice best fits this topic?
options: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
questions.answer_key: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.
questions.explanation: Deterministic build steps: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action. Apply the guidance to the actual event, runner, permissions, or artifact boundary and test the relevant case.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to improving workflow reliability?
options: Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Reliable workflows use deterministic dependency versions, explicit timeouts, idempotent deployment steps, bounded retries, and tested recovery paths. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
